summary: Defines extensions to the CDNI Metadata and Footprint and Capabilities Advertisement interfaces for the Open Caching use case, where a commercial CDN is the upstream CDN and an ISP caching layer is the downstream CDN.

eli5.summary: A big video company and a local internet provider cooperate. This helps them tell each other which requests to handle.

questions: how do open caching cdns exchange metadata
what is a redirect target in cdni
what is the cdni fallback target
subtitle: How a commercial CDN and an ISP caching layer tell each other where to redirect viewers, and where to send them back.

tldr.problem: In the Open Caching use case, a commercial CDN wants to hand video requests to an ISP caching layer, but needs a way to learn the ISP's redirect addresses, which vary by region and change over time, and the ISP needs an address to send requests back to.
tldr.mechanism: The ISP (downstream CDN) advertises a Redirect Target capability object over the Footprint and Capabilities Advertisement interface. The commercial CDN (upstream CDN) supplies a Fallback Target metadata object over the Metadata interface.
tldr.outcome: Requests can be redirected by DNS CNAME or HTTP redirect to the ISP cache and bounced back to a fallback address when the cache cannot serve them. Both objects are registered as CDNI Payload Types.

today: RFC 8804 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2020, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the CDNI metadata and footprint specifications in RFC 8006 and RFC 8008.

sections.title: Open Caching and CDNI
sections.content:
The Open Caching Working Group of the Streaming Video Alliance focuses on handing video delivery requests from commercial Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) to a caching layer in the ISP's network. In Content Delivery Network Interconnection (CDNI) terms, the commercial CDN is the upstream CDN (uCDN) and the ISP caching layer is the downstream CDN (dCDN).

This RFC defines two objects needed for Open Caching request routing: a Redirect Target capability, which the dCDN uses to advertise where the uCDN should redirect clients, and a Fallback Target metadata object, which the uCDN uses to tell the dCDN where to send clients back. The first travels over the Footprint & Capabilities Advertisement interface (FCI, RFC 8008) and the second over the Metadata Interface (MI, RFC 8006). The extensions come from Open Caching requirements but are also applicable to CDNI use cases in general.
sections.eli5: A video company sends viewers to a local helper so the videos arrive faster. This document says how they swap the addresses they need to do that.

sections.title: The Redirect Target Capability
sections.content:
In iterative redirection (RFC 7336), the uCDN must know an address, the Redirection Target (RT), to send clients to at the dCDN. Those addresses can vary by footprint, for example between regions, and can change over time, for example after network problems. That makes them unsuitable for bootstrap-time configuration, so the RFC uses the FCI, following a suggestion in RFC 7336.

Two reasons are given for a dynamic interface. For footprint, a dCDN spread across several geographies may want a different target per footprint; a single name with Geo DNS has limits, since a client may use a third-party resolver. For scaling, the dCDN may add request routers in new locations and advertise them.

A target may be attached to one uCDN host, a list of hosts, or all hosts. When the dCDN names hosts, it MUST list them as redirecting-hosts, and the uCDN may redirect to that address only if the request was to one of those hosts. An empty or missing target means no target is available, and if one was advertised earlier, the update deletes it.

For DNS redirection the target is an FQDN used as the alias in a CNAME response from the uCDN's DNS router. When the EDNS0 client-subnet option is present, a uCDN SHOULD prefer routing by client subnet, and a dCDN using it MUST be aware of the privacy drawbacks in RFC 7871. For HTTP redirection the target is the URI used in the Location header of a 3xx response, typically 302 (Found).
sections.eli5: The local helper tells the big company, 'for these shops, send people to this address.' The address can change, so the helper keeps updating the list.

sections.title: Target Objects and Properties
sections.content:
The Redirect Target capability object has three properties, all optional: redirecting-hosts (a list of Endpoint objects; if absent or empty the target applies to all hosts of the uCDN), dns-target and http-target. The capability type is FCI.RedirectTarget.

A DnsTarget object has one mandatory property, host, a hostname or IP address without a port number. If a port is present, the uCDN MUST ignore it.

An HttpTarget object builds the redirect URI:

  • host (mandatory): hostname or IP address with an optional port.
  • scheme: either http or https. If absent, the uCDN uses the scheme of the original request.
  • path-prefix: ends with a trailing slash, and the original path is appended after it.
  • include-redirecting-host: a Boolean, default false. When true, the uCDN redirecting host is added as a path segment before the original path.

In the RFC's example, a request for /vod/1/movie.mp4 at a.service123.ucdn.example.com is answered with a 302 whose Location is https://us-east1.dcdn.example.com/cache/1/a.service123.ucdn.example.com/vod/1/movie.mp4.
sections.eli5: The address is built like a recipe: the helper's name, an optional folder, and then the original path. A few switches say whether to add the original shop's name too.

sections.title: The Fallback Target
sections.content:
The dCDN sometimes cannot handle a request. Open Caching therefore has the uCDN provide a fallback target server. To avoid redirect loops, its address MUST differ from the original uCDN address the client was redirected from, and the uCDN MUST avoid further redirection when a request arrives there.

The RFC lists three use cases. Failover: a dCDN request router has no caches to route to, due to failures or temporary overload. No coverage: the client is in an area the dCDN caches do not cover, or outside its footprint. Error: a cache cannot properly serve a request, for example because some metadata was not acquired.

The Fallback Target is a generic metadata object of type MI.FallbackTarget, carried inside the host-metadata property of each uCDN host. It has a mandatory host (for DNS delegation it SHOULD NOT include a port, and the dCDN MUST ignore one) and an optional scheme, which must be http or https. For HTTP redirection back to the uCDN, the dCDN must use the original URL path, stripping any dCDN path-prefix or uCDN hostname it had been given.

The uCDN SHOULD design for the case where a large part of the dCDN fails or is under denial-of-service attack and sends many requests back to it. Using a different fallback address for each uCDN host lets it load balance them like its original hosts.
sections.eli5: If the local helper cannot answer, it sends the visitor back to a special back door at the big company. That back door must never send them to the helper again, or they would go in circles.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
The extensions inherit the security and privacy considerations of the Metadata Interface and the FCI. The RFC adds that the Redirect Target capability object may reveal information about the internal structure of the dCDN network, and a third party who intercepts FCI transactions could use it to attack the dCDN. The Fallback Target object likewise may reveal the internal structure of the uCDN.

Implementations of the FCI and MI therefore MUST use strong authentication and encryption, following the directions for securing the Metadata Interface in RFC 8006.
sections.eli5: The address lists show how each company is laid out inside, so they are passed in sealed, signed envelopes and not on open postcards.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered two CDNI Payload Types in the registry defined by RFC 7736: FCI.RedirectTarget (interface FCI, encoding in the Redirect Target section) and MI.FallbackTarget (interface MI/FCI, encoding in the Fallback Target section). The purpose of each is to tell the object apart from other advertisements.
sections.eli5: The two new kinds of messages each get an official name in the shared list, so everyone recognizes them.
